differences.what: the pedestal's front and west faces: the base, plinth and die at the camera's fourteen fitted corners, 10.5 px rms, the largest residual 22 px (0.1 m) on the mouldings

the pedestal's depths: the west faces show the base 2.85 m, the plinth 1.8 m and the die 1.6 m deep; built 3.3, 2.3 and 1.9 m (reconstructed) until this camera measured them [T-3568: the record's depths set to the reading and the monument rebuilt]
the die's west panel, a narrow bronze plate on the west face: drawn in the render in place
the cap's profile: two stepped washes and a fillet in the print, one slab over a cove in the render, its overhang within 0.15 m
the plinth's top moulding and the die's base moulding: drawn in more steps in the print than the render's single fillet, under 0.1 m

the front panel's tone: fresh dark bronze, darker than the new granite, in this 1893 print; since T-3589 the render draws the panels pale, as ICHi-19208 shows them about 1900 with their relief weathered light. The two pictures disagree because seven years of weather stand between them, and the 1904 scene takes the later one

the lettering under the front panel, three lines of pale cut letters: not cut in the render [T-3589: cut since, three lines read on ICHi-19208, which fall here under the panel at the print's place and size]

the warrior (left): in the print he lunges to the left, crouched, his weight on a bent right leg with the left stretched back, his body twisted toward the woman and his head at Black Partridge's shoulder, the tomahawk raised over his head in his right hand and a feather in his hair; the render stands him upright on straight legs, so his head and the tomahawk's head stand about 0.35-0.4 m higher than the sculpture's and his stride is lost [T-3582: re-posed joint by joint on this picture: the lunge to the left on the bent right knee with the left leg stretched back to the rock's west edge, the body twisted to the woman with the head down at Black Partridge's shoulder, the tomahawk raised in the right hand with its head below the grip, the left arm across to her, the feather in his hair and the fringed ornament at his left hip]

Margaret Helm (centre): in the print she staggers, leaning back against Black Partridge, her head turned, her right arm reaching across to the warrior, her dress falling in folds to the rock with a cloak loose behind; the render is an upright figure in a smooth cone of skirt with her arms out to the sides [T-3582: re-posed on this picture: leaning back against Black Partridge, the right arm across to the warrior's waist, the left hand back at Black Partridge's chest, the hair in a knot, the skirt falling to the rock and the cloak hanging from the right arm; the folds themselves are T-3583's]

Black Partridge (behind her, right): in the print his left arm is raised high and out to the upper left with the palm open against the blow, his head in a headdress with a long feather streaming back, the musket slanting down past his right side; the render raises a straight arm ending in a long bar and carries a stick at his right, without the open hand, the headdress or the musket's shape [T-3582: re-posed on this picture: the left arm raised high and out to the upper left ending in an open hand, the feather standing from the headband and the long one streaming back, the right arm round Mrs. Helm, the musket slanting from behind the left shoulder past the right hip to its butt, the stride to the right]

the post surgeon (under them): in the print he lies across the front of the rock under the woman's skirt, his legs out toward the child; the render is a low lump with a ball for a head at the woman's left [T-3582: re-posed on this picture: half-lying back across the rock under Mrs. Helm's skirt, his head at the warrior's bent knee, propped on one arm, one leg stretched out to the west edge (the second picture shows it reaching the foot beside the warrior's; the reading 'legs toward the child' was the old record's)]

the child (right front): in the print he kneels at the rock's right edge reaching out with both arms; the render stands him upright in a cone with one arm out [T-3582: re-posed on this picture: kneeling at the rock's edge, both arms reaching out to the right]

the rock: a rough, broken mound rising under the figures' feet in the picture; a low smooth swell in the render [T-3582: a broken field of many small lumps over a few large ones, every point knocked up or down a few centimetres, rising under the feet; its ledges are the generator's, not the cast's stone by stone]

the faces, hair, dress and undress, ornaments and weapons as sculpted: since T-3588 the bodies are the people rigs (hm08, posed to the joints read here), so each figure has a body, hands, feet and a head with the rig's neutral face and short hair, and the warrior and Black Partridge their rigs' breechcloths, Black Partridge his leggings, Mrs. Helm her rig's gown, the surgeon his coat and pantaloons and the child his jacket and trousers, all cast in the one bronze; none of it is yet modelled to the sculpted faces, hair, drapery, ornaments and weapons (T-3589, L-fort-dearborn-monument-3567)

the group's outline as a whole: the print's rises from the rock at about y 690 to the tomahawk at y 175 (orig. px) and spans x 350-830; the render's spans x 330-900 and its tomahawk stands at y 135, the warrior's upright stance and Black Partridge's long bar (above) [T-3582: the five figures re-posed (above), so the render's outline now follows the print's figure by figure; what is left is the group's height, below]
the estate wall and its coped pier behind at right, and the young street tree: not drawn by this review

the group's height through this camera: every joint of the figures reads 25-85 px higher in the print than in the render, and the rock's top 25-30 px, at any depth a joint could stand at (T-3582 tried them all), so through this camera the group is about 10 per cent taller than through ICHi-19208 (about 2.35 m of figures against 2.13). The two camera fits disagree: this one is fitted on the base, plinth and die alone, below the group; ICHi-19208 is the square-on view the record takes (form.group_h_m says both)

the figures' masses: since T-3588 each figure is a posed people rig, not tapered limbs and balls; the warrior's long lunge, Black Partridge's raised hand and the child's kneel read through this camera as bodies. Still open (T-3589): Mrs. Helm's dress is the rig's slim gown inside the cone of skirt the poses kept, the folds and the cloak smooth masses; Black Partridge reads straighter and squarer than the print's
